subject: CAIQ custody plan and artifact escrow logistics
messages:
From: Alice Mercer <alice.mercer@cloudharbor.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security@cloudharbor.com
Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2027 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: CAIQ handoff / custody for artifacts

Hi Irene —

Thanks again for the quick demo last week. Our security team wants to proceed with a CAIQ review but has two asks before we kick off:

1) A control mapping file (CSV/Excel) that ties Redwood's CAIQ answers to the CSA controls, with artifact pointers and owner names.
2) A short custody plan covering long-term retention of sampled runtime artifacts (logs, telemetry snippets) that our auditors may request. We prefer an external escrow/transfer process when artifacts need to be preserved beyond your standard retention window.

Can your team send a draft mapping and a proposed escrow template? Ideally we get something by EOD Wednesday so our auditors (Dan Liu) can schedule sampling.

Thanks,
Alice Mercer
Director, Security Programs
Cloud Harbor, Inc.

Attachments: none
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Mercer <alice.mercer@cloudharbor.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2027 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: CAIQ handoff / custody for artifacts

Alice —

Appreciate the clear asks. Quick plan from our side:

- We will produce a CAIQ->CSA crosswalk in Excel that includes: question id, our short answer, control mapping, owner, and a pointer to the evidence artifact (doc name + path).
- For sampled runtime artifacts, we will propose two paths: (A) temporary export to a secure S3 bucket we manage with time-bound access, or (B) an escrow package we prepare and ship to an approved third-party vault (PDF manifest + encrypted bundle).

Marissa will lead the crosswalk and Ben will draft the escrow/retention template. We can deliver the first drafts by EOD Wednesday PST. Does that timeline work for your auditors?

Irene Choi
Head of Security & Compliance (on rotational coverage)
Redwood Inference

--
Irene Choi
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Mercer <alice.mercer@cloudharbor.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Nov 2027 08:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: CAIQ handoff / custody for artifacts

Alice / Irene —

Attaching the initial CAIQ->CSA mapping (caiq-mapping-draft.xlsx). It includes a first-pass owner column and where to find the artifact in our internal evidence repo. Notes:

- I left cells with question-level ambiguity highlighted in yellow; those need technical confirmation from Jonas/infra.
- For runtime logs we list two representative artifact types: ephemeral request traces (sampled) and batch telemetry exports (periodic). Both have different retention rules.

Ben has attached a short Artifact Escrow Template (artifact-escrow-template.pdf) that outlines: scope of artifacts, encryption/transfer process, custody handoff steps, and a suggested retention escrow window (90–365 days depending on sensitivity).

Next steps we propose:
- Jonas to confirm the highlighted mappings (by EOD Thursday).
- Alice / Dan to confirm which artifact categories they may sample so we can prepare exports.
- If Cloud Harbor needs the escrow route, we'll initiate the DocuSign/transfer authorization flow (HS-9876543).

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: caiq-mapping-draft.xlsx, artifact-escrow-template.pdf
From: Dan Liu <dan.liu@auditpartners.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Alice Mercer <alice.mercer@cloudharbor.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Nov 2027 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: CAIQ handoff / custody for artifacts

Thanks all — I reviewed the draft mapping and the escrow template. A few quick remarks from the audit side:

- The mapping looks comprehensive; I only flagged three items where the control rationale doesn't clearly tie to a persistent artifact (questions: 3.2.1, 5.4.7, 10.1.3).
- For the escrow approach, the encrypted bundle + manifest approach is acceptable, but we need the manifest to include SHA-256 checksums and the exact extraction command used for runtime samples (so results are reproducible).
- Suggest a 180-day default escrow window for logs tied to live incidents; other telemetry can be 90 days.

Alice: we'll indicate which categories we intend to sample by Friday. Once indicated, Marissa/Ben, please prepare a sealed bundle and share the Drive link and HS record.

Dan Liu
Principal, Audit Partners LLC
